items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We rehearsed this show and opened in a town called Oxford, Ohio... Hoskin gave us some sort of sad story about the money... we told Hoskin that we had done our last show for him.

ctx.x: The next time I saw Joe Smith, he was with Fletcher Henderson, but that's another story and I shall speak about it later.

Shortly after the Chocolate Dandies show left Cincinnati, a fellow by the name of Hoskin came to town and contacted Trotter for some musicians to accompany a show that he was going to produce. This show was to play quite a few small towns in the state of Ohio and maybe a few in Indiana. It was natural that Trotter told Hoskin that he had some musicians. Hoskin had a young violinist with him. We rehearsed this show and opened in a town called Oxford, Ohio, which was not far from Cincy. I don't recall if the show…

There was a young man living in Oxford who became quite friendly with the musicians. His first name was Theodore and he was the first person I had ever known who was a negro but looked like a white person. He came with us when we left Oxford just to be with the show. We played a theatre in Middletown, Ohio and we told Hoskin that we wanted Theodore to sit in the ticket office with the other person that would be selling tickets for the show that night. We had our first full house that evening and after it was over…
